claim: A UCP maintainer notes a checkout ID does not by itself bind authorization to a checkout state (doc line 908). Ledger AC#351 instead says UCP main gained a return policy extension (2026-10-23), a completion boundary rule (2026-11-07) and a purchase options and subscription policy (2026-11-10).
corrected: Body text stands. PR 1057, merged 2026-11-07, states "A checkout ID does not by itself bind authorization to a particular checkout state." The ledger row AC#351 names a return policy and subscription policy that this PR does not mention. Reword it to: UCP PR 1057, merged 2026-11-07, clarifies the completion boundary.
why: One bullet in a list of UCP gaps. No ranking or recommendation depends on it.

claim: ACP requires Idempotency-Key and API-Version on POSTs, uses a bearer token, and offers a detached JSON signature header for requests (ledger AC#153). Doc line 387 also cites it for P12 detached JWS over canonical JSON and HMAC. Doc line 314 says optional HMAC signature for webhooks.
corrected: ACP requires Idempotency-Key on all POSTs and API-Version, uses a bearer token, and has an optional Signature header described as an HMAC signature for webhook verification. The spec file does not mention JWS, detached signatures or canonical JSON. Line 314 is right. On line 387, drop R1-07 from the detached JWS value and keep it only for HMAC. Fix ledger AC#153 to match.
why: A cell in the protocol comparison matrix. Line 314 already carries the correct wording.

claim: About 50 to 60 of 423 open x402 issue titles concern dispute, refund, receipt or proof (doc lines 712, 1615). Ledger AC#321 says 60 of 423 titles mention dispute, refund, receipt, proof, attestation or delivery.
corrected: About 50 of 424 open x402 issue titles (count on 2026-11-15) mention dispute, refund, receipt, proof, attestation or delivery. Whole word matches give 48 and word stems give 51. The four words dispute, refund, receipt or proof alone give 41. The count is live and moves.
why: It is the only numeric evidence for the no proof of delivery challenge (rank 13) and the matching objection line.
